messages:
deploybot: Attempting soft-unpin of runtime v4.0.0 for model-group 'summarizer-xl' detected drift in canary routing. Soft-unpin paused automatically at 14:07 UTC. Reason: 11% of requests still routed to pinned variant due to sticky affinity on dedicated pools. See /deploy/logs/2938475610.

alex: quick context: we rolled runtime v4.0.0 last night; canary looked clean for 45m but some dedicated customers remained on the pinned v3.9.5 because of per-customer affinity. Unpin should be cautious.

tia: affinity is the issue — dedicated pools with customer pinning aren't respecting the new routing because their pinlist entry is explicit. If we force-unpin, we risk flipping dedicated customers unexpectedly.

sre-oncall: risk assessment: forcing global unpin when 10% of traffic is still on pinned hosts could cause state mismatch for evicted sessions. Propose: convert soft-unpin to staged-unpin: 1) remove canary pins, 2) keep dedicated pool pins until manual opt-out by customer or until agent upgrade confirms compatibility, 3) set TTL 24h for dedicated pin entries.

legal: flag: we need to check contract SLAs for dedicated customers before changing runtime behavior. Some enterprise contracts require 72h notification for non-security-impacting changes. Please confirm before widening.

docs: also flag for release notes: if we leave dedicated pinned, we need two separate notes: hosted customers (unpin happened) and dedicated/private (still pinned). We should avoid confusing language. I'll draft two short bullets.

opsbot: Scheduled action: staged-unpin window provisioned 20:00-22:00 UTC. Playbook RB-42 queued for manual approval. Auto-escalation disabled for dedicated pools.

alex: proposed plan: 1) complete hosted unpin now (canary->hosted) since hosted metrics are stable, 2) convert dedicated pins to staged state with TTL 24h and notify account owners, 3) run host-agent upgrade on dedicated pools during the 20:00 window to clear affinity, 4) if any dedicated pool reports >1% error or p95 +250ms, abort and keep pin.

tia: technote for account owners: add a one-liner they can run to opt-in earlier: ```rbctl set-runtime --pool <pool-id> --runtime 4.0.0 --force-opt-in``` Use with caution — will break in-flight sessions.

sre-oncall: monitoring thresholds: hosted unpin rollback trigger = errors >0.6% (5m) OR p95 increase >200ms (10m). Dedicated pools: immediate page if any pool reports host-compat <99% after agent upgrade.

legal: confirm: we'll send account owners a 24h heads-up and mark the change as non-breaking in comms. OK to proceed with staged approach once docs + account messages are ready.

docs: drafting two release-note bullets now and a short account email template. Will post for review in 15m.

alex: executing hosted unpin step now. Monitoring live metrics. Will post status in 30m.

deploybot: Hosted unpin complete at 14:15 UTC. Dedicated pool pins converted to staged with TTL 24h. Staged-unpin maintenance window scheduled 20:00-22:00 UTC. Playbook RB-42 requires manual approval to clear staged pins.

opsbot: Alerts configured and account notifications queued. If RB-42 triggered for rollback, run rollback playbook RB-17 for hosted and RB-43 for dedicated reverse orchestration.

sre-oncall: I'll keep dashboards open and escalate on thresholds. Tagging this for post-mortem and runbook updates after the window.
